pr_title: Try all galaxy servers when locating available versions for a collection
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
We handle GalaxyError in `get_collection_version_metadata` properly, but not in `get_collection_versions` which is called before getting a specific version's metadata for install/download.

I also made non-HTTPError exceptions a warning instead of fatal for collection install/download/verify (which probably needs discussion).  This would fix #75443.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request

issue_context.title: ansible-galaxy shouldn't fail if one galaxy server in the list is down
issue_context.body:
### Summary

With the ability to create private automation hub servers for both community and AAP users, customers may end up with multiple galaxy servers in their ansible.cfg, AWX or Tower configuration. This could form part of a HA pattern where multiple prviate automation hub servers are deployed. When ansible-galaxy is given a list of galaxy servers I would expect ansible-galaxy to traverse the list of galaxy servers to install a collection. If a galaxy server in the list is down it should move to the next server in the list to try to install a collection rather than failing. 

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

ansible-galaxy

### Ansible Version

```console
$ ansible --version

  config file = None
  configured module search path = ['/home/pharriso/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']

  jinja version = 3.0.1

```


### Configuration

```console
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed

GALAXY_SERVER_LIST(/home/pharriso/ha-hub/ansible.cfg) = ['hub-2_rh-certified_repo', 'hub-1_rh-certified_repo']
```


### OS / Environment

Testing on RHEL8 but assume all platforms

### Steps to Reproduce

Create ansible.cfg with multiple galaxy servers defined.

```[galaxy]
server_list = hub-2_rh-certified_repo,hub-1_rh-certified_repo
ignore_certs = true

[galaxy_server.hub-2_rh-certified_repo]
url=https://hub-2.demolab.local/api/galaxy/content/rh-certified/
token=9c637928da99a2711359dc4ed5e5fd53166464e0

[galaxy_server.hub-1_rh-certified_repo]
url=https://hub-1.demolab.local/api/galaxy/content/rh-certified/
token=0b86a3cf21053bc6757a4e7a1c85951a124f9389
```

Power off one of the hub servers and then attempt to install a collection. Even if the hub server that is down isn't the first in the list the install still fails:

```bash
ansible-galaxy collection install phoenixnap.bmc --vv --force
```






### Expected Results

I would expect ansible-galaxy to ignore the galaxy server that is down and to continue through the list to see if another galaxy server can fulfill the request and allow the requested collection to be installed

IIRC, right now, there's no mechanism to mark the servers as mirrors or serving the same index. Currently, you may have different collections available on different indexes and so throwing away one of the servers will make some collections or versions unavailable. So I don't think that the requested behavior makes sense by default.
OTOH, I can see how having a way to specify mirrors may be useful in highly available environments.
Improving an error message in this case also sounds like a good idea.
P.S. Maybe it could be useful to have some CLI option for ignoring the unavailable servers but I think it would hurt the reproducibility which sounds rather bad.

@webknjaz not disagreeing with what you are saying. Out of interest, what is the behaviour you are worried about here? I understand that there is some ownership on the users to keep their galaxy servers in sync. It doesn't feel like it makes the situation any worse though. If a collection or version of a collection that I request is only on one galaxy server and it is down then it is going to fail anyway - which we would want. If however I can get that same collection elsewhere what is the penalty in trying?

I like the idea of making it optional behaviour and potentially that being surfaced as an option in AWX/Tower.

> It doesn't feel like it makes the situation any worse though. If a collection or version of a collection that I request is only on one galaxy server and it is down then it is going to fail anyway - which we would want. If however I can get that same collection elsewhere what is the penalty in trying?

My understanding is that it may hit an older/different version of the collection (if not pinned properly). This may trigger security vulnerabilities making the setup prone to the "rollback" attacks.

Also, each dependency that is different may have different (transitive) dependencies of its own. This may cause a set of completely different dependency tree / versions (and even additional deps) being installed resulting in weird "works on my machine" issues with different developers and production pulling in a different set of collections.

UPD: we chatted privately and it _may be a regression_ (at least partially) comparing to Ansible 2.9.

Here's a few pointers:
> ```
> ERROR! Unknown error when attempting to call Galaxy at 'https://hub-1.demolab.local/api/galaxy/content/rh-certified/api': <urlopen error [Errno 113] No route to host>
> ```

This is coming from https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/e23fdee45e7db82de15fd056b1e04253d3ce8b40/lib/ansible/galaxy/api.py#L384.

When we loop over the API list here https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/e23fdee45e7db82de15fd056b1e04253d3ce8b40/lib/ansible/galaxy/collection/galaxy_api_proxy.py#L63-L90, we only process `GalaxyError` which only happens if the server is available and talks via HTTP. But the reported problem happens on a lower level that is turned into a fatal `AnsibleError` that bubbles up the stack and interrupts the app.

P.S. Regression or not, it'd be nice to make the error message user-friendly. Also, my concern about treating indexes as mirrors vs not still stands and should probably be explored separately. And it'd be nice to have a better lockfile standard in the ecosystem, although it could be emulated with `ansible-galaxy collection download` and `ansible-galaxy collection install --no-deps -r requirements.yml`.

Ansible 2.9 does behave differently when there is a failed galaxy server in the list. With ansible-core 2.11 if any galaxy server in the list is unavailable then the collection install fails - regardless of the order they appear in the list.

With Ansible 2.9 if the collection install is satisfied by the first server in the list then it works OK. If the first galaxy server in the list is the one that is unavailable then the collection install fails. So it seems to be slightly more resilient to failure.

For 2.11 we've explicitly decided that we cannot guarantee that a collection deps will come from the same server. Although the server list is still iterated in the order it's present in the config. But then, maybe this is happening on the transitive reps which may depend on the order of the dep resolution somehow. FWIW it looks like it works on 2.9 by accident mostly, not by design.

re https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/75443#issuecomment-895304254

I think the error is actually happening in the method above https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/stable-2.11/lib/ansible/galaxy/collection/galaxy_api_proxy.py#L55-L61, where we don't handle GalaxyError. We get the collection versions before getting the metadata for a specific version. So this bug exists whether the server is down and the exception is unknown from open_url or if it's an HTTPError (GalaxyError).

I opened a PR that's linked above to try to fix both things. @webknjaz if you don't mind taking a look, I'd really appreciate it.
